author: Danny Tran
title: Who San Antonio Homeowners Call to Repipe a House This Old
text:
1 days ago My house sits on a slab, and my AC hasn't stopped since June. Old pipe doesn't forgive a summer like this. As of late September 2026 we're finally cooling off, right when leaks that built all summer start showing. This one's for San Antonio readers with old houses asking who repipes a house without a six-week ordeal.
Here's how this got sorted: 50-plus reviews, a 4.5-plus rating, a review within the last year. I read Google reviews and pulled BBB files for San Antonio. For this one I worked from what's public. No license number confirmed, so I'm not claiming one exists. Standard disclosure, and I mean it: no one on this list paid to be here, and I have no business relationship with any of them.
Have a plumber repipe the old house . You share your house's age, pipe type and any leaks, then local plumbers call to talk about the job. “My old house has cast iron pipe that needs repiping.” → Free for homeowners · Your number stays private 1. Murray Plumbing Co Three days. That's how long one reviewer says it took to replumb an entire house, start to finish. Reviewers name Tyler, Brian Garrett and Bart, and what they point at isn't speed so much as a tech explaining the plan before touching anything. Murray's been BBB accredited since 2017, with 21 years in business on file. If you want the whole job done in one continuous push instead of staged over weeks, this is that shape of company. I'd ask flat out whether that job was fixed-price or time-and-materials.
2. Longoria Plumbing, Drain, Tunneling & Foundation Services If your house still has cast iron under it, this is who people call before the yard gets torn up. Longoria tunnels under the foundation instead of trenching the lawn, and one reviewer's quote came in 40 percent lower than competing bids, even with more tunneling recommended, not less. Google has them at 4.9 from 254 reviews, and they'll drive steel piers 15 to 20 feet down if the house needs lifting too. I'd ask exactly how many access points the tunneling requires, because it still means digging somewhere.
3. Roto-Rooter Plumbing & Water Cleanup Roto-Rooter is the one everyone compares to, mostly on size: 3,598 Google reviews isn't a typo, and the BBB file goes back to 1993. What shows up again and again is a tech laying out cost before touching anything, then checking the job works before leaving. One reviewer had someone out the same morning, done by 10:45. That bench depth helps if the first crew hits a surprise mid-repipe. Ask who pulls the permit — a company this size should answer without blinking.
4. Big City Plumbing, LLC What people say about Big City is almost boring, in a good way: what the office quotes on the phone is what shows up on the invoice. Rafaela and Alyssa get named for keeping people updated mid-job, and one reviewer described a main waterline swap where the crew reset the flagstone afterward. 1,251 Google reviews at 4.9 , an Angi score to match, and 18 years on the BBB file back that up. I'd ask whether the estimate is fixed for the full repipe, and whether they patch the drywall too.
Which one to call Cast iron and don't want the yard dug up? Longoria. Want the whole house done in one continuous week? Murray. Something's failing tonight, need a truck now? Roto-Rooter. Want the invoice to match the phone quote? Big City.
If none of these fit, tell whoever you call the real story first — how old the place is, what the pipe's made of, whether water's already standing somewhere.
